comment: Expected behaviour of every case that runs in minutes.  A change that
moves any of these numbers is a change in the answer and has to be
justified by a measurement, not by the fact that the next wall passed.
Numbers were re-recorded on 1 thread after loadpath.c made grip-to-grip
connectivity a per-increment census and made severance end the run; they
are trajectory quantities, so an A/B must fix OMP_NUM_THREADS and
MKL_NUM_THREADS on both arms (runs are NOT reproducible across thread
Several cases USED to record a longer trajectory.  Every increment that
disappeared was past the point where the specimen had come apart: the
deletion sets are unchanged and every status line up to severance is
byte-identical to the pre-change baseline.  What was dropped is phantom,
required_lines: every run's log must contain these, so a report that silently stopped being emitted is caught.

cases.name: fast-plain
cases.what: the bar with a partial cohesive plane: bulk damage, deletion, cutbacks, ending where the specimen actually comes apart.  It used to run to increment 507 and theta=1: all 90 deletions are complete by increment 65 and the 442 increments after it were two halves joined by failed facets, reporting a load that rose linearly from 1.2% to 6.5% of peak

cases.name: fast-plain-smooth
cases.what: the regulariser on a deck with real bulk damage and 90 deletions where no DAMAGED facet ever closes: it must be a byte-for-byte no-op, because the blend differs from the sharp law only when g<1 AND the facet is in compression

cases.name: fast-wrapped
cases.what: the eroding phase wrapped in facets: reaches a node with no bulk support, and comes apart at increment 96.  The kink wall this deck is famous for is at increment 99, theta=0.158766 - three increments and 0.005% of load factor PAST severance, which is why fast-wrapped-wall has to ask for it explicitly

cases.name: fast-wrapped-smooth
cases.what: the same deck with the crack-face kink regularised: it comes apart at theta=0.159500 against the sharp arm's 0.158758, a shift of 7.4e-04 - the same figure already recorded as the largest shift in any deletion time, measured a second way.  It used to record increment 515 and theta=1, which was 420 increments past severance

cases.name: fast-wrapped-nospc
cases.what: the same specimen without the load-path mask, which must not change where it comes apart

cases.name: fast-wrapped-wall
cases.what: the crack-face kink wall itself, kept as a regression by asking to run past severance. rc=201 at increment 99, theta=0.158766, is the exact pre-change number - so the wall is unchanged, and now it is on record that it is a convergence failure of a specimen that came apart at increment 96

cases.name: fast-wrapped-wall-smooth
cases.what: the same, with the kink regularised: the wall is gone and the fracture is not, the pre-change result (increment 515, theta=1) reproduced exactly.  Both arms are past severance from increment 96 and 94 respectively, so this pair measures the regulariser, not the specimen

cases.name: mixed-analytic
cases.what: inclined cohesive plane against the closed-form post-peak branch, 36 percent shear.  Stops at theta=0.5 where both facets have failed and the two halves separate; the 2400 post-peak increments the benchmark exists to check all lie before that

cases.name: mixed-analytic-smooth
cases.what: the same, with the kink regulariser armed: that facet never closes, so it must be bit-identical

cases.name: close-sharp
cases.what: the UC6 normal law itself, verified point by point on a facet damaged to gmin and then closed: this is where the five-orders tangent jump is measured rather than argued.  It is two blocks joined by two facets and nothing else, so it is severed in tension by design at increment 42 and needs CCX_FRACTURE_PAST_SEVERANCE to reach the compressive step that is the point of the test

cases.name: close-blend
cases.what: the same facet under the regulariser: identical far-field slopes, so nothing physical moved, and the blend band actually exercised
